overall_assessment: The contract evolution and schema migration framework established in contracts/migrations/registry.json, contracts/migrations/github-issue-hierarchy-v1-to-v2.json, and scripts/check_schema_migrations.py enforces rigorous backward-compatibility and fail-closed governance. The migration registry binds default policy constants requiring unknown_version: reject, destructive_migration: deny, implicit_write_upgrade: deny, backup_required: true, and receipt_required: true. Automated unsupervised migration is disabled by contract (automatic_migration: false). For multi-version schema families such as github-issue-hierarchy, minimum read versions are anchored to preserve historical payload readability (v1 read-only) while restricting current write operations to the highest validated schema version (v2). Migration plan github-issue-hierarchy-v1-to-v2 declares explicit non-destructive transformations, preserves all source node keys and hierarchy identities, mandates pre-migration backups, and includes a reversible rollback strategy (project_v2_to_v1_projection). The validation script scripts/check_schema_migrations.py scans all 73 catalog entries, validates multi-version family parity, and outputs structured receipts with zero errors.
verified_invariants: fail-closed schema registry policy: default policy mandates unknown_version: reject, destructive_migration: deny, and implicit_write_upgrade: deny
no automated migration: registry specifies automatic_migration: false and individual migration plans specify automatic_apply: false
non-destructive migration: all schema migration plans enforce destructive: false
backup and receipt requirement: schema migrations require prior state backups and emit verifiable receipts before synchronisation
read-backward compatibility: minimum read version must preserve the oldest catalog version for multi-version families
write-version pinning: write operations are pinned strictly to the highest catalog version
declarative rollback support: all migration plans define explicit rollback.supported: true and documented loss reports
catalog and migration parity: script verifies exact correspondence between schema-catalog multi-version families and registered migration plans

findings.description: Schema migration plans and registry policies are declaratively validated; executable migration and rollback drivers applied to representative persisted datasets in production storage remain an open maturity gate.
findings.recommendation: Preserve gate T26-G-DATA-MIGRATION-DRILLS open until automated persistent storage migration runners are integrated.

findings.description: Migration plan github-issue-hierarchy-v1-to-v2 explicitly details downstream rollback semantics, identifying that task-level native relationships are dropped in v1 projection while preserving canonical v2 source nodes.
findings.recommendation: Adopt this explicit loss reporting pattern for all future forward/backward schema projections.

findings.description: scripts/check_schema_migrations.py validates catalog naming conventions (*.v<N>.schema.json) across all 73 schemas and verifies that migration plans move strictly forward (from_version < to_version).
findings.recommendation: Retain regex-based schema catalog naming enforcement in pre-commit and validation gates.

Schema deprecation rules, fail-closed unknown version rejection, non-destructive migration invariants, and rollback contracts verified.

calibration_notes: Contract evolution specialists confirm that schema evolution policies, non-destructive migration rules, rollback specifications, and catalog validation tooling meet all structural requirements. Executable persisted-data migration drills remain an open gate.
claim_boundary: Source-verified implementation only. Declarative schema catalog history, non-destructive migration plans, rollback contracts, and fail-closed policies are verified; compiled data migration drivers and production storage rollback drills remain open gates.
